newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock mutual funds rose 14 percent, says Lipper.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock mutual funds rose 14 percent, says Lipper.

text.p: Investors were again in love with stock mutual funds in the second quarter as the average U.S. stock fund jumped nearly 14 percent, a firm that tracks the fund industry reported Tuesday.

Lipper Analytical Services Inc. said a preliminary report covering March 31 through June 12 showed that all mutual funds sectors, other than gold, racked up gains in the latest quarter, and they were also up for the year.

The firm said the average stock fund rose 13.7 percent for the quarter and the increase more than made up for the slight loss in the first quarter. The sector was up 11.4 percent since the start of the year.

Financial services funds -- those with investments in banks and related businesses -- were the best-performing funds in the quarter, Lipper said, with a gain of 15.9 percent. Year-to-date, the group was up 18.5 percent.
Investors continued their preference for funds with investments in big-name companies, it said, noting that Standard & Poor's Index funds were up 17.0 percent.
The gold-oriented funds were off 5.0 percent in the second quarter and lost 12.5 percent for the year.
Funds that invest in science and technology companies had a strong quarter, with an increase of 13.8 percent but world equity funds fell 1.97 percent, it said.
Among world equity funds, there was a resurgence of Japanese funds, which rose 19.3 percent, surpassing the continued upbeat performance of Latin American funds, which posted a rise of 15.6 percent.
But overall, Japanese funds are still down 11.6 percent for the year, Lipper said.
